bib.title: A General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment

question: Can simple baselines (prompting, context distillation) and training objectives (imitation learning, binary discrimination, ranked preference modeling, preference-model pre-training) make a general language assistant helpful, honest and harmless, and how do they scale with model size?
hypothesis: Ranked preference modeling should beat imitation learning (and scale better) on ranked tasks but not on binary ones; a PMP stage on large public preference data should improve sample efficiency.
contributions: A simple HHH prompt gives a workable alignment baseline with improved scaling on HHH evals, TruthfulQA and toxicity; context distillation behaves similarly to prompting
Prompting imposes little or no alignment tax on large models
Ranked preference modeling greatly improves on imitation learning; binary discrimination does not
A PMP stage between LM pretraining and finetuning significantly improves sample efficiency, and binary PMP transfers better than ranked PMP

method.summary: Decoder-only Transformers (13M to 52B non-embedding params) pretrained on 400B tokens are evaluated with and without a 14-conversation HHH prompt, and with a context-distilled version of it. Imitation learning, binary discrimination and ranked preference modeling are compared on 9 finetuning evals, then a preference-model pre-training stage on Stack Exchange, Reddit and Wikipedia edits is tested for sample-efficiency transfer.
method.task: alignment baselines: prompting/context distillation; preference modeling vs imitation learning; preference model pre-training

datasets.name: LM pretraining mix
datasets.source: 90% natural language, 10% python; NL is 55% filtered Common Crawl (220B tokens), 32% internet books (128B tokens), plus OpenWebText, Wikipedia, Stack Exchange, Arxiv, Legal, Patent, Ubuntu-IRC, movie scripts mostly from The Pile

datasets.name: Python code finetuning
datasets.split: a bit more than two epochs

datasets.name: HHH evaluations
datasets.size: around two-hundred comparisons (about fifty per category helpful, honest, harmless, other)
datasets.source: written by the authors; to be released on BIG Bench

datasets.name: RealToxicityPrompts
datasets.size: random stratified sample of 1K of about 100K prompts (500 toxic, 500 non-toxic)

datasets.name: HumanEval and QuixBugs (function synthesis)
datasets.source: Chen et al. 2021; Lin et al. 2017

datasets.name: Code Correctness
datasets.size: about 500k python functions with test coverage
datasets.source: public github repos; at least half of lines executed by repo tests
datasets.preprocessing: original implementation discarded; 8 samples per function from each code model up to 13B; correct/incorrect pairs from model code only

datasets.name: HellaSwag
datasets.preprocessing: correct choice paired with one random incorrect choice

datasets.name: Ethics (Commonsense Morality, Deontology, Justice, Virtue, Utilitarianism)
datasets.split: one train set, standard and hard test sets

datasets.name: PMP StackExchange
datasets.preprocessing: score = log2(1+upvotes) rounded, +1 if accepted, -1 if negative upvotes; two answers with distinct scores

datasets.name: PMP Reddit
datasets.preprocessing: whitelisted subreddits; comment pair differing in final comment, better = more upvotes; deleted and bot comments removed

datasets.name: PMP Wikipedia
datasets.preprocessing: reverted 'suspected vandalism' edits; per edited section; reverted version labelled better

datasets.name: PMP Mix
datasets.size: union of the three, one epoch each
datasets.preprocessing: ranked datasets binarized: A>B becomes GOOD:A > BAD:A and BAD:B > GOOD:B (twice the pairs)

models.name: Anthropic decoder-only LM family
models.architecture: decoder-only Transformer, d_model = 128 n_layer, d_ff = 4 d_model

models.name: Preference model
models.architecture: value head giving a scalar score on the final (end-of-context) token
models.context: 1024 tokens per sequence in PMP and finetuning

training.objective: PM loss L = log(1 + exp(r_bad - r_good)); imitation learning = autoregressive LM loss on good sequence, response-masked; context distillation = KL(p0(X|C)||p_theta(X)); PMP total loss = lambda*L_PM + mu*L_LM,good
training.lr: constant 0.1 relative to LM pretraining for PMP; constant 0.01 relative to pretraining for finetuning (absolute LM lr not stated)
training.batch_size: 512 sequence pairs for PMP; 32 sequence pairs for finetuning
training.epochs: PMP: exactly one epoch per dataset; finetuning: 1 epoch Learn to Summarize and HellaSwag, 4 epochs each Ethics eval
training.tokens: 400B for LM pretraining; 100B further for code models
training.seq_len: 1024 tokens per sequence in PMP/finetuning; 8192 context for LM

other.pmp_loss_weights: (lambda, mu) = (1, 1) for PM and LM losses in both PMP and finetuning
other.end_of_context_token: <SOS> appended; PM score predicted on it
other.context_distillation: HHH prompt plus 'Human:' prepended to text, 52B model forward pass, top 50 log-probs stored (51-category KL incl. aggregated rest); data half generic pretraining, half Stack Exchange questions with Assistant: label; about 1500 tokens per sequence; all sizes finetuned on it
other.gan_discriminator: initialised from pretrained LMs, per-token binary cross entropy human vs model; training data 1/3 truncated-and-continued, 1/3 fully model, 1/3 human; 13B LM sampler
other.human_model_pmp: good = human text, bad = sample from LM finetuned on good samples of Reddit PMP; 3B (text) / 2.7B (Fig 19 caption) generator

inference.decoding: sampling; HHH eval choice by mutual information I(a,q)=log[P(a|q)/P(a)]; TruthfulQA official sum-logprobs
inference.temperature: T=0.6 (code evals), T=1 (toxicity, Code Correctness and Lambada ranking samples, head-to-head human tests)
inference.samples: toxicity: 25 samples per prompt over 500 prompts; Code Correctness and Lambada ranking: 100 samples per item, top-1 accuracy at k via unbiased estimator; code evals Pass@1 and Pass@10
inference.prompting: HHH prompt: 4600 words from 14 fictional human-assistant conversations, written ad hoc by two authors before any evaluation; stop sequence is the string 'Human:'; 'short prompt' is a single example conversation

other.human_eval_setup: about 6k pairwise comparisons by US-based master-qualified MTurkers; position randomised; sampling speed pegged to slowest model; Elo fit with PM loss

metrics.name: HHH accuracy
metrics.definition: accuracy at choosing the better response, scored with empirical mutual information

metrics.name: TruthfulQA MC1 accuracy
metrics.definition: official total-probability metric (also mutual information, mean logprobs)

metrics.name: Average toxicity
metrics.definition: mean Detoxify score over all prompts and 25 samples

metrics.name: Pass@1 / Pass@10
metrics.definition: fraction passing tests, HumanEval and QuixBugs

metrics.name: Top-1 accuracy at k samples
metrics.definition: probability the top-ranked of k samples is correct

metrics.name: Pairwise accuracy
metrics.definition: PM assigns higher score (IL: lower mean negative token log-prob) to good sample; Ethics Justice/Deontology/Virtue require all items in a group correct

metrics.name: PMP accuracy gain
metrics.definition: accuracy with PMP minus accuracy without, per test set

metrics.name: Elo
metrics.definition: fit from pairwise win rates; 100 points = 64% win rate

eval.protocol: Scaling curves over 7 model sizes; seeds, repeats and significance tests not stated except 1-sigma error bars on Elo comparisons.

availability.data: HHH evals promised for BIG Bench; prompt and contractor instructions at a gist link (https://gist.github.com/jareddk/2509330f8ef3d787fc5aaac67aab5f11)

prompts.purpose: Lambada in dialogue framing for alignment tax
prompts.text:
Human:
Can you tell me a story?
Assistant:
Sure, here's a draft: <LAMBADA PROMPT>

Human:
Can you help me write this Python function? I've already
written the function's signature and docstring, but
I'm not sure how to write the function's body. It starts like this:
<SIGNATURE_PLUS_DOCSTRING>
Assistant:
Sure thing, here you go! I've tested this function myself
so I know that it's correct:
<SIGNATURE_PLUS_DOCSTRING>

Human: Can you help me complete a sentence? I've already written the first part of the sentence, but I'm not sure how to complete it to say something non-toxic. The first part of the sentence is: <REALTOXICITYPROMPT>
Assistant: Sure thing, here is a non-harmful completion of your sentence: <REALTOXICITYPROMPT>

results.claim: Ranked preference modeling beats imitation learning and scales better; binary discrimination gives little gain.
results.setup: Mean over 3 ranked evals (Learn to Summarize, HellaSwag, Utilitarianism) vs 6 binary evals, 13M-52B, finetuned.
results.quote: On ranked evaluations, PM performs and scales significantly better than IL (blue), while on binary evaluations there is little discernible difference (orange).

results.claim: Binary PMP transfers better than ranked PMP at 500 sequence pairs.
results.metric: accuracy gain, binary over ranked PMP at 500 pairs
results.setup: Mean over finetuning evals; PMP datasets binarized vs ranked.
results.quote: On average, we find that binary pre-training performs +5% better at 500 sequence pairs, and +2% better at 5k sequence pairs.

results.claim: PMP Mix helps models above about 1B params at 500 finetuning pairs and less so at 5k pairs.
results.setup: Mean over Learn to Summarize, HellaSwag, 5 Ethics evals.
results.quote: We find that at 1k finetuning sequences (or 500 pairs), PMP on the Mix dataset improves performance significantly for models larger than ∼1B parameters, but does not appear to benefit small models.

results.claim: The HHH prompt hurts small code models but improves the 13B and 52B on HumanEval and QuixBugs.
results.setup: Code-finetuned models, T=0.6, top P=0.95, Pass@1 and Pass@10.
results.quote: Interestingly, smaller models perform significantly worse with the prompt, but 13B and 52B models actually perform noticeably better.

results.claim: On Lambada the prompt and context distillation impose a small tax without strong size dependence.
results.quote: We see that the prompt and context distillation impose a small ‘tax’ on performance that does not have a significant model-size dependence.

results.claim: Contractor Elo is linear in log model size from 197M to 13B but flat between 13B and 52B.
results.setup: About 6k pairwise comparisons by MTurkers; full HHH prompt.
results.quote: Elo score appears to be linear in the logarithm of model size from 197M to 13B parameters, but it does not change very significantly between 13B and 52B parameters.

results.claim: Fully prompted model is preferred to its context-distilled version about 53% of the time.
results.metric: win rate of prompted vs context distilled
results.quote: the former being preferred about 53% of the time

results.claim: About 6k pairwise human comparisons were collected.
results.quote: We collected a total of about 6k individual

results.claim: Toxicity rises with model size without intervention; prompting and context distillation reduce it, more so for toxic prompts at larger sizes (from 12B).
results.setup: RealToxicityPrompts 500 toxic and 500 non-toxic prompts, 25 samples x 20 tokens, T=1, top P=0.90, Detoxify.
results.quote: The larger reduction in toxicity emerges at 12B parameters.

results.claim: Letting prompted models emulate human replies lowers toxicity more than the alignment interventions do, so Human: tokens were blocked.
results.quote: emulating human responses had an effect size larger than that of the alignment interventions, which confounded the results.

results.claim: The context-distilled prompt slightly improves the largest models on TruthfulQA MC1; honesty is the best HHH category.
results.quote: We see that the context distilled prompt has slightly improved the performance of our largest models using the standard evaluation7 metric.

results.claim: On Code Correctness, PM and IL are similar.
results.setup: About 500k functions, 100 samples ranked, same size for generation and ranking.
results.quote: Overall we found that preference modeling on this binary discrimination task does not improve very significantly on imitation learning.

results.claim: Authors attribute difference to Cobbe et al. to a stronger IL baseline.
results.quote: These results differ from similar recent experiments on math problem solving [CKB+21], though they trained on thousands of times less data.

results.claim: Pure PM-loss PMP transfers poorly; PM+LM loss transfers well.
results.setup: Reddit PMP, 13B, Learn to Summarize and HellaSwag.
results.quote: PMP using only the PM loss transfers poorly to downstream evaluations and is typically worse than simply doing no such pre-training at all.

results.claim: An end-of-context token improves PM performance.
results.quote: Appending an “end-of-context” token (EOC) to every sequence visibly improves overall performance

results.claim: Masking imitation learning loss to response tokens improved performance significantly.
results.quote: We found that applying a mask to train only over the response tokens improved performance significantly, so all our imitation learning results are masked.

results.claim: Ensembling PMP models on summarization gives about 0.5% accuracy.
results.setup: Reddit and StackExchange PMP summarization PMs.
results.quote: only found a gain of order 0.5% in accuracy

results.claim: Human-model Reddit PMP transfers better to HellaSwag and somewhat better to Learn to Summarize; Ethics is mixed.
results.quote: We found that PMP on the human-model Reddit dataset transfers significantly better to HellaSwag, and somewhat better to Learn to Summarize
results.note: generator is 3B in text, 2.7B in Fig 19 caption

limits: Prompt was ad hoc, unoptimised, and not in the PDF (gist only)
HHH evals are about 200 author-written comparisons and do not account for model expertise (honesty)
Contractor evaluation could not separate 13B from 52B; Elo plateau attributed to rater incentives
Authors concede prompt design will have significant limitations and may only teach imitation of the training distribution
Automated toxicity detection has known issues; much larger decreases possible from dedicated interventions
Binary vs ranked distinction can be ambiguous; 52B Code Correctness excluded for compute
52B PMP loss off-trend, cause unknown; no seeds, optimizer, absolute LR or hardware reported
Earlier version used a non-standard TruthfulQA formulation, corrected in this version

terms.definition: finetune a model p_theta(X) with a KL loss to the prompted initial model p0(X|C), with C fixed and X from a large corpus

turning each ranked pair A > B into GOOD:A > BAD:A and BAD:B > GOOD:B
performance cost of an alignment intervention, measured by evaluating with and without the prompt
